TIME EXTENSION NO. 2026-02
A request by IDI Logistics to extend entitlements for Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No.
2023-01 and Precise Development Plan (PDP) No. 2022-03 for one final year to allow for
a logistics facility within a new 76,602 square foot industrial building, including associated
site improvements at 14516 Carmenita Road (Assessor Parcel Nos. (“APNs”) 8069-001-
032, 8069-001-033, 8069-001-034, and 8069-001-035).

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Senior Planner Salazar presented background information on the applicant’s request for
a final one-year time extension. He stated that on July 12, 2023, the Planning
Commission approved Conditional Use Permit No. 2023-01, Precise Development Plan
No. 2022-03 and Lot Merger No. 2022-01 to allow a logistics facility within a new 76,602
square foot industrial building, including associated site improvements; that pursuant to
the California Environmental Quality Act Guidelines Section 15332, the project was
determined exempt; that the applications became effective on July 24, 2023, after the ten
calendar day appeal period had elapsed; that on July 24, 2024, staff approved a one-year
time extension, and on July 24, 2025, approved a second one-year time extension.

Further, Senior Planner Salazar stated that the applicant’s letter dated May 4, 2026,
requesting a third and final one-year time extension, referred to the fact that market
conditions for industrial buildings in Los Angeles County have declined and leasing rates
have decreased.

In response to Commissioner Macias’ comment on the applicant’s letter pertaining to the
current market conditions, the applicant’s representative, Aaron Scherer, (participating
remotely), shared that they have a team that works with tenants and brokers; that they
are looking for “built-to-suit”; that it seems like the market is starting to improve and that

Request:

The applicant, Joshua Laureano, is requesting approval to establish and operate an Indoor
Recycling Facility at 1,725 square foot (sq. ft.) in size, which will accept empty beverage containers
for recycling purposes (California Redemption Value) (Proposed Use).

Entitlements Requested:
  •  Director Approval Request No. 2026-06 requesting approval to allow the unclassified use of
  an indoor recycling facility as a conditionally permitted use pursuant to Norwalk Municipal
  Code (NMC) Sections 17.02.204 and 17.02.203.C.1.k.
  •  Conditional Use Permit No. 2025-02 requesting approval to establish and operate of an
  indoor recycling facility (buyback center) within an enclosed 1,725 square foot building

  located within an existing 4.16-acre shopping center pursuant to NMC Sections and
  17.02.210 and 17.04.110.
Recommendation:
  That the Planning Commission:
1. Adopt Resolution No. 26-07, to approve Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2026-06 subject
  to Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
2. Adopt Resolution No. 26-08, to approve Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2025-02 subject to
  Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and
3. Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) Guidelines pursuant to Section 15303 (Class 3 – New Construction or Conversion of
  Small Structures).
Authority:

Section 17.02.203.C.1.k of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) authorizes the Director to make
determination regarding unclassified uses, pursuant to NMC Section 17.02.204. The Director may
refer any request to the Planning Commission for review and determination.

Section 17.04.110 (Recycling facilities) of the NMC requires that a CUP be filed for recycling
facilities which accept empty beverage containers for recycling purposes, to establish a set of
regulations to control the time, place and manner of operations of such centers and to prevent
detrimental impact on surrounding uses.

Section 17.02.210.A of the NMC authorizes the Planning Commission of the City of Norwalk
(“Planning Commission”) to grant a Conditional Use Permit (“CUP”) for those uses which are so
allowed by the Zoning Ordinance and impose certain conditions as it deems necessary and
reasonable to protect the best interests of the surrounding property or neighborhood and to ensure
compliance with the general purpose and intent of the Zoning Ordinance and the Norwalk General
Plan.
Introduction/background:

The Subject Site located at 10921 Rosecrans Avenue (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Numbers
[APNs] 8052-001-038 and 8052-001-039), is located within the Crawford’s Plaza Shopping Center
which is 4.16-acres in size and has a General Plan land use designation of Neighborhood
Commercial and zoning classification of Restricted Commercial (C-1).
The Subject Site is located on the northwest corner of Studebaker Road and Rosecrans Avenue
within the Crawford’s Plaza shopping center. The site is bound by Van Ruiten Street to the north,
Studebaker Road to the east, Rosecrans Avenue to the south, and single-family residences to the
west.

Project Description:
Site Plan
The subject site is located within an existing 4.16-acre multi-tenant shopping center which is
anchored by Superior Grocers as the major tenant. There is a total of three commercial buildings
on the site totaling 111,000 sq. ft. of floor area. The remainder of the site is designed with surface
off-street parking stalls and landscaping (see Attachment D).

Floor Plan
The tenant space will be approximately 1,725 sq. ft. in size with direct customer access from the
shopping center walkway along the building frontage. See Attachment D for the floor plan. A “Buy
Back Exchange Area” at 835± sq. ft. in size is proposed as the area where customers enter the
business to exchange their recyclable items in exchange for monetary value. Towards the rear of
the tenant space, a temporary storage area, office, and restroom are provided. This area will be
provided with a drain to empty the liquid contents of the recyclable items. This area is separated
from the Buy Back Exchange area with a solid wall.

Site Circulation & Parking
There are four vehicular access points for ingress and egress (one on Van Ruiten, one on
Studebaker Road, and two along Rosecrans Avenue) to the shopping center, the nearest vehicular
access point to the subject tenant space is located on Rosecrans Avenue. The site currently has
200 parking spaces. It is the applicant’s intent to secure off-street parking spaces in front of the
tenant space to be designated for customers’ loading and unloading of recyclable items for
redemption.

Based on information provided by the applicant, staff determined that the parking ratio should be
calculated at one space per 250 sq. ft., consistent with retail parking requirements. According to
City business license records, the tenant space was previously occupied by a barber shop that
ceased operations on December 31, 2024, and maintained the same parking requirements.

Business Operations
The proposed recycling buyback center will operate from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday to
Saturday and will be closed on Sundays. The facility will be staffed by two full-time employees and
will provide California Redemption Value (CRV) services for aluminum cans, glass, and plastic
bottles. No other materials will be accepted. Customers will be responsible for disposing of any
unaccepted materials off-site; however, designated waste bins will be provided and emptied daily
by employees to ensure proper site maintenance. No recyclable materials or waste will be stored
on-site overnight.

Operationally, customers will access the facility through the front entrance, where employees will
inspect and sort materials brought in for recycling. Eligible and non-eligible materials will be
separated accordingly, with non-eligible items properly disposed of off-site. Recyclable materials
will be weighed using a scale approved by the California Department of Food and Agriculture,
Division of Measurement Standards, ensuring compliance with applicable State requirements.

Customers will be encouraged to empty liquid contents prior to redemption. A floor drain system will
be installed within the enclosed building to dispose of incidental residual liquids from recyclable
materials. The system will be designed to handle minimal liquid discharge and will comply with all
applicable local, county, and state regulations.

At the end of the business day, a loading truck will pick up the bins storing the recycling items
collected and exchange with empty and clean bins. The operations statement is provided in
Attachment D.

Safety and Security
Conditions of approval are recommended to require a surveillance system, lighting, and participation
of the Department of Public Safety's Business Watch program and anti-trespassing/enforcement
program (S.H.A.P.E.). Calls for service (see Attachment E) is included which describes the calls for
service for the shopping center for the past six (6) years.
Analysis:

Indoor recycling facilities are not listed as a specific permitted use in the NMC. Since not all land
uses can be expressly identified in the Zoning Code, nor can all future uses be anticipated, Chapter
17.02.204 of the NMC, authorizes the Director to make determinations regarding unclassified uses
based on required findings and may approve such uses when found to be consistent with the intent
of the Zoning Code and General Plan.

Pursuant to Table 17-A (Land Use Matrix) and Chapter 17.04.110 of the NMC, Recycling Facilities
are described as mobile recycling facilities and reverse vending machines and are permitted subject
to the approval and continued validity of a CUP in specific zones. In addition, such uses must be
located within a designated “convenience zone,” defined as an area within a one-half-mile radius of
a supermarket with gross annual sales of at least $2,000,000.

Based on the information provided by the Applicant, the proposed indoor recycling was determined
to be comparable to recycling facilities that are permitted with a CUP pursuant to NMC Section
17.04.110 (mobile recycling facilities and reverse vending machines). The proposed use accepts
empty beverage containers for recycling purposes. Recycling Facilities are conditionally permitted
within commercial zones.

General Plan Consistency
The Neighborhood Commercial land use designation is intended to allow commercial, retail, and
service uses that serve the essential daily needs of surrounding residential areas. Supermarkets,
drug stores, household goods stores, and personal services are examples of uses that are
consistent with this land use category.
One of the goals of the City of Norwalk General Plan Land Use Element is to identify community
needs and incorporate necessary community-serving facilities into the fabric of the city. The
proposed indoor recycling facility is consistent with the Neighborhood Commercial designation, as

it provides a convenient and accessible service to nearby residents by facilitating the proper disposal
and recycling of household materials. This use supports daily neighborhood needs by promoting
environmental sustainability and reducing the need for residents to travel outside the area for
recycling services. Additionally, because the facility will operate within an enclosed building in an
existing shopping center, it is compatible with the scale and character of surrounding commercial
uses.

Zoning Compatibility
In conjunction with approval of a DAR for unclassified uses, the proposed indoor recycling facility is
comparable to the Recycling Facilities uses conditionally permitted within the C-1 zone. It is not
expected to generate greater impacts related to traffic, parking demand, noise, glare, odor, or refuse
than other permitted commercial uses. The proposed operation would have similar hours of
operation and is not anticipated to be substantially more intensive in terms of employees, customers,
or overall activity. According to City business license records, the tenant space was previously
occupied by a barber shop, which ceased operations on December 31, 2024.

The proposed indoor recycling facility also meets the State “convenience zone” requirement, as it
is located within one-half mile of a qualifying supermarket. This proximity enhances accessibility
and supports the intended purpose of providing convenient recycling opportunities for residents.

Recycling Facilities Context
Further, the City of Norwalk currently has one recycling-related facility with an active business
license. This facility operates as a portable recycling center located approximately 2.2 miles from
the subject site within an existing shopping center in the General Commercial (C-3) Zone.

The proposed project would expand access to recycling services by providing a permanent
facility in closer proximity to surrounding residential neighborhoods, thereby improving
convenience and supporting the City’s sustainability goals.

Public Notification:

Public hearing notices were published in The Norwalk Patriot on June 26, 2026, and posted at
locations set forth in NMC Section 1.08.030 as well as mailed to 166 property owners within 500
feet of the property. As of the writing of this report, staff have not received any correspondence
regarding the proposed project.

Environmental Assessment:

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the project is categorically exempt
from environmental review under Section 15303 (Class 3 – New Construction or Conversion of
Small Structures) of the CEQA Guidelines. This exemption applies to the conversion of existing
small structures from one use to another where only minor exterior modifications are involved. The
proposed project consists of establishing a recycling facility within an existing commercial building,
with minor interior modifications currently proposed. Therefore, no further environmental review is
required.
Summary:

Staff recommends approval of the request to establish and operate an indoor recycling facility,
subject to the conditions outlined in the attached resolutions. These include, but are not limited to
restricting operating hours and requiring that the recycling facility and surrounding area be
continuously maintained in a clean and aesthetically pleasing condition. The proposed location of
the facility will not be visually obtrusive and is not expected to generate noise impacts on
surrounding commercial or residential properties.

Although an indoor recycling facility is not specifically identified as a permitted use in the NMC, it
may be considered substantially similar to recycling facilities (mobile recycling facilities and reverse
vending machines) which are conditionally permitted uses within the C-1 zone through the DAR
application for unclassified uses. The required findings for approval of a DAR for unclassified use
and a CUP for an indoor recycling facility are provided in Resolution No. 26-07 and 26-08
respectively.

If the Planning Commission approves DAR No. 2026-06, indoor recycling facilities may be
considered permissible in the C-1, C-3, C-M, M-1, and M-2 zones, subject to review and approval
of a conditional use permit. Future requests for such facilities will be evaluated on a case-by-case
basis in accordance with applicable provisions of the NMC.

The proposed use will comply with all applicable regulations and, as conditioned, will not be
detrimental to public health, safety, or the welfare of surrounding uses. The project is consistent
with the General Plan’s vision of providing adequate local-serving commercial uses.

  Section 3. Director Approval Request Findings. All necessary findings for the

  17. Hours of operation for the Proposed Use - due to immediate proximity of residential
  housing, to protect the “quiet enjoyment” of the nearby residences, the hours of
  operation shall be limited to 10:00 A.M. to 4:00 P.M. (Monday-Saturday, closed on

  18. Daily site sanitation - the operator must perform daily comprehensive cleaning of
  the premises and the immediate exterior perimeter (to include affected parking
  areas) to remove debris, spills and abandoned items related to their recycling
  center.

  19. Odor mitigation - the installation and maintenance of professional-grade odor
  control systems or strict containment protocols to ensure no smells emanate into
  the adjacent residences, adjacent retail spaces, the centers shared walkway or the
  public right-of-way.

  20. Collected recyclable material shall be stored indoors. No overnight storage of
  returned aluminum cans, glass, and plastic bottles or waste is permitted.

  21. Any fluids collected from recyclable materials shall be disposed of within an
  appropriate drain within the building. Fluids may not be dumped on the parking lot
  or other adjacent areas.

  breaking, and loading/unloading of materials during business hours.

  required for the tenants. Stalls shall be located in front of the tenant space in which
  the Proposed Use is located.

  interfere with the through-traffic or fire lanes. Operator shall create and post a
  “Zero-Staging” policy where no materials (bags, glass or scrap) can be placed or
  left in the ground of the parking lot or the adjacent sidewalk areas. All materials
  must move directly from the vehicle to a self-contained bin or the interior of the
  unit.

27. Queue management and loitering control - The operator shall be prohibited from
  allowing customers to line up or stage on the sidewalk or in the parking lot more
  than 15 minutes before opening. Install, “No Loitering / No Lining Up Before

  The operator shall be responsible to maintain pavement repairs or be required to
  install reinforced concrete “pads” in the stalls they use for loading to prevent
  asphalt rutting.
